scene_summary: Weathered green-gray architectural relief on a pale ground: a monumental cropped wheel dominates the upper left, a detached rosette sits at right, and two carved strata cross the lower image. Recessed petals, nested rims, punctures, grooves and broken section edges offer real interaction anchors. The composition is restrained in palette but ornate rather than minimal or expressionist.
usable_surfaces: Exposed crescent of the monumental wheel's outer rim
Dark upper-right recessed face inside the large wheel
Three circular punctures in the middle horizontal relief
Compressed curved grooves in the bottom stratum
Upper petal cavity of the detached right rosette
Stepped upper edge of the middle relief
Broken upper groove in the bottom stratum

detected_objects.label: Worn nested rim
detected_objects.visual_evidence: An exposed crescent of thick, chipped outer molding follows the large wheel's right and lower perimeter. Its granular green-gray surface is separated from the inner aperture ring by narrow curved grooves. The polygon selects this rim, not the wheel's entire bounding area.

detected_objects.label: Sheltered inner cut
detected_objects.visual_evidence: A broad charcoal-colored wedge recess lies above the rightward spoke of the monumental wheel. Raised radial walls and a rounded outer end visibly shelter its mottled recessed face.

detected_objects.label: Sparse lower punctures
detected_objects.visual_evidence: Three distinct dark circular holes occupy a small raised capsule along the upper edge of the middle relief. The contour hugs the shared punctured ridge and excludes the adjacent large floral medallion. This is a visual anchor only; it does not resolve the provisional source identity.

detected_objects.label: Compressed incision seam
detected_objects.visual_evidence: Several closely nested curved seams descend beside the dark round cavity in the bottom relief. Their narrow parallel channels provide a visible compressed seam, although the plate does not show an extensive field of dense rhythmic incisions. Source identity and playback remain unverified.

detected_objects.label: Stepped end notch
detected_objects.visual_evidence: The middle relief's raised upper section ends in an abrupt step near the image center, descending into a shallow horizontal ledge. The polygon follows the worn solid lip of the step rather than the empty ground above it. It is an upper-edge notch, not an isolated terminal end face.

detected_objects.label: Interrupted lower groove
detected_objects.visual_evidence: A broken, scooped-out upper edge interrupts the top contour of the bottom stratum, leaving a low ochre-green trough between taller relief sections. The selected contour follows the exposed material at the break. The interruption is visibly ragged rather than a clean machined dropout.

detected_objects.label: Interrupted lower groove
detected_objects.visual_evidence: Planned source surface fallback used because plate inspection returned fewer mapped objects than source bindings.

complexity_assessment.rationale: Approximate visual coverage. The cropped wheel, detached disc and two horizontal relief strata establish a legible hierarchy, with open ground separating the upper forms. Repeated petals, apertures, nested moldings and distressed texture make the plate ornate and moderately busy rather than minimal or expressionist. Most mapped anchors remain distinct, but the detached rosette cavity is small and the lower seams compete with neighboring carving.

mapping_note: Package assembly filled unmapped source pockets from planned artifact surfaces because plate inspection returned too few detected objects.
